content.title: About
content.content: Yellow raw peaches (Peaches, yellow, raw) are juicy fruits of the peach tree (Prunus persica) grown in temperate climates. They have a sweet aroma, tender flesh and a mildly tangy flavor. Peaches are usually eaten fresh, used in desserts, salads and beverages.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peaches belong to the Rosaceae family and are closely related to plums, apricots and cherries.
The skin of yellow peaches is rich in antioxidants, especially carotenoids that give the fruit its bright color.
Since ancient times, peaches have been a symbol of longevity and abundance in Chinese culture.
Peach pits contain amygdalin, which can convert to cyanide when processed; therefore the pits are not eaten raw.
In the United States more than 1.5 billion pounds of peaches are produced each year.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Peaches provide a good amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber in peaches promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium contributes to normal heart function and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Carotenoids and flavonoids in yellow peaches protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene, which converts to vitamin A, benefits vision.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peaches, ranging from skin rash to swelling.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Peaches contain natural sugars, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Seeds
items.content: Peach pits contain amygdalin, which can form cyanide; they should never be eaten raw.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peaches can be eaten fresh, sliced into salads, added to yogurt, smoothies, baked goods, or cooked into compotes. The skin can be left on for extra nutrients or peeled according to preference.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store peaches at room temperature until fully ripe, then refrigerate. In the fridge they keep for 3–5 days. Avoid airtight containers, which can speed up overripening.
